To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a transgene controlled under ubiquitin (Ub) promoter is expressed in undifferentiated human embryonic stem (ES) cells and in ES-derived hematopoietes and endothelial cells, and is capable of forming vasculature in a sprouting embryoid body (EB) model.
a lentiviral transgene under ubiquitine promoter is expressed in undifferentiated and differentiated hES cells.

lentiviral transduction of hES cells with GFP under ubiquitin promoter resulted in stable GFP expression during prolonged cultivation, and GFP-H1 cells were capable to form hematopoietic colonies and tubular structures in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of lentiviral vectors to transduce genes into hES cells.
a novel strategy for genetic modification in hESC.
the development of lentiviral vectors and their applications in hES cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of ubiquitin promoter for lentiviral transduction of human ES cells is an effective strategy for stable and durable expression of transgenes in hES cells and hES-derived hematopoeitic and endothelial cells.
lentiviral vectors are suitable for stable genetic modification of hESC, and that the ubiquitin promoter is a useful tool for stable gene expression during hESC differentiation.
the ubiquitin promoter is a useful and effective tool for stable genetic modification of hESC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lentiviral vectors can be used for genetic modification of hESC and the transgene expression can be retained under the control of the ubiquitin promoter during hES cell development.
lentiviral transduction of hES cells is a useful tool for genetic manipulation and gene therapy.
the ubiquitin promoter in the lentiviral transgene vector is able to express the reporter gene in undifferentiated and differentiated hES cells.

a transgene controlled by ubiquitin promoter is expressed in undifferentiated H1 hES cells and their hematopoietic/endothelial progeny, and the lentiviral vector is an effective tool for genetic modification of hESC for cell-based therapies.
the ubiquitin promoter can be used for long-term gene expression in hES cells.
